text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Finance Minister Christodoulos Christodoulou uses harsh language to dismiss inaccurate claims by the opposition on the state of the economy.
- It is natural for icons to cry -- but it is not a miracle, says a scientist.
- Military talks between the two sides under the auspices of the United Nations reach a breakthrough.
- Tension, what tension? President Glafcos Clerides dismisses British and U.S. concerns about increased tension in Cyprus.
- Laughable claims by the finance minister. The scare caused by the meningitis outbreak is to blame for the state of the economy!
- President Clerides plans to meet with the chairman of the right-wing Disy party Yiannakis Matsis in an attempt to settle internal disputes in the party.
- Cyprus's electricity authority is today expected to endorse a tender for the purchase of generators for its new power station.
